outcome: Composite primary outcome (preeclampsia, gestational diabetes, or preterm birth before 32 weeks)
cohort: 487,870 women with singleton (n = 480,010) and twin (n = 7860) pregnancies in Ontario, Canada, between April 2012 and March 2016
finding: The association between maternal obesity and adverse pregnancy outcomes, such as preeclampsia, gestational diabetes, and cesarean delivery, is weaker in twin pregnancies compared to singleton pregnancies.
mod_finding: In twin gestations, underweight (but not overweight or obesity) was associated with the greatest risk of preterm birth at < 32 weeks, mainly due to an increased risk of spontaneous preterm birth.
